tryThisNow: Open a calendar block and write one owner-audit note for a holding: what cash was distributed, what earnings were retained, and what management must justify.

implementationPlan.title: Run a Dividend Owner Audit
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Use a two-minute owner audit before accepting management's capital policy. Check whether you are acting like an owner, whether retained earnings have a clear justification, and whether dividend policy affects income and capital-allocation evidence.

ifThenPlans.plan: If a price move is the only item in your calendar block, then add one owner-rights line covering residual claims, voting rights, proxy materials, and director elections.

If management retains earnings without a clear explanation at the front desk of your review, then mark the decision pending until the retained earnings case addresses shareholder distributions and comparable value.
If your budget app treats dividends as separate from valuation, then move payout policy into the return note and ask whether retained earnings and capital redeployment justify the trust.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Before the next day ends, choose one holding and complete a two-minute audit note with three lines: owner rights, retained earnings justification, and dividend policy as part of return.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: During a weekly calendar review, repeat the same audit for one active holding. Leave any decision pending when management keeps profits without a clear owner-facing reason or when payout policy is ignored.
